## Concept {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part 1</div>
<div class="section-title-text">Concepts of reproducible, AI-assited project workflows</div>


## Motivation

- Reproducibility is a hallmark of good science
- A well-organized, reproducible project often makes work more efficient
- AI supported work is the future (present)


## Problems with "standard" workflows

::: {.problems-layout}
::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>Results drift from their code</strong><span>Copied tables and figures become hard to update or verify.</span></div>
<div><strong>Files lose their roles</strong><span>Raw, processed, current, and obsolete versions become difficult to distinguish.</span></div>
<div><strong>Decisions disappear</strong><span>Cleaning and modeling choices remain in memory or private conversations.</span></div>
<div><strong>Sharing becomes risky</strong><span>Private data and unfinished material move into unsuitable places.</span></div>
<div><strong>Reproducibility is hard</strong><span>Others (including your future self) will struggle reproducing your work.</span></div>
:::

::: {.problem-figure}
![](./media/amiracleoccurs.gif){fig-alt="A black-and-white cartoon showing an unexplained step labeled 'Then a miracle occurs' in a mathematical derivation."}
:::
:::

::: {.notes}
[Sources] Cartoon supplied by the project owner: media/amiracleoccurs.gif.
:::


## The ORDERly concept

<p class="figure-lead">Organized + Recorded + Documented + Executable = Reproducible (**ORDER**ly).</p>

::: {.flow-figure .orderly-flow}
<div class="flow-row">
<div><strong>Organized</strong><span>predictable<br>places</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div><strong>Recorded</strong><span>changes<br>and decisions</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div><strong>Documented</strong><span>purpose<br>and instructions</span></div>
<p>+</p>
<div><strong>Executable</strong><span>saved steps<br>that run</span></div>
</div>
<div class="flow-down-arrow">↓</div>
<div class="flow-outcome"><strong>Reproducible</strong><span>a stated result can be recreated</span></div>
:::


## AI support needs to be managed

- Organization
- Restrictions
- Documentation
- Evaluation

can preserve reproducibility.




## Human judgment remains the gate

::: {.simple-list .spacious}
<div><strong>Science</strong><span>Are the data, model, assumptions, and interpretation appropriate?</span></div>
<div><strong>Governance</strong><span>May these data, documents, and systems be used with this AI tool?</span></div>
<div><strong>Acceptance</strong><span>Does the change work, and can the project owner explain and defend it?</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
AI can support judgment but cannot transfer accountability. Never send private or restricted material to an AI tool unless that use is explicitly approved.

[Sources] Local template: ai/ai-use-policy.md; data/readme-data.md; agents.md.
:::

## Implementation {.section-break}

<div class="section-kicker">Part 2</div>
<div class="section-title-text">Implementation</div>
<div class="section-subtitle">A setup to support an AI assisted ORDERly workflow.</div>


## The components

- A structured template (as GitHub repository)
- A set of tools that support ORDERly workflows
- Tools are largely interchangable, but text-based, easy to track tools are best (avoid Excel, Word, etc.)


## Specific tools

- IDE, e.g. Positron, VS Code, RStudio
- Coding language(s), e.g. R, Python, Julia
- Authoring software, e.g. Quarto or Typist
- Tracking tools, e.g. Git/GitHub
- Agentic AI tools, e.g. ChatGPT Codex, Claude Code





## The repository structure gives each part a role

<p class="figure-lead">The main path moves through data, code, results, and products; support folders provide stable inputs and guidance.</p>

::: {.flow-figure .repository-flow}
<div class="flow-row primary-flow">
<div><strong>data/</strong><span>inputs<br>derived data</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>code/</strong><span>workflow<br>stages</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>results/</strong><span>generated<br>outputs</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>products/</strong><span>deliverables<br>for audience</span></div>
</div>
<div class="support-row">
<div><strong>assets/</strong><span>stable<br>support</span></div>
<div><strong>docs</strong><span>readme<br>usage</span></div>
<div><strong>ai/</strong><span>policy<br>summary<br>log</span></div>
</div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Walk through the main path first. Then add assets for supporting materials and ai for policy, context, guidance, and meaningful-use records.

[Sources] Local template: readme.md; usage.md.
:::

## Separate raw, derived, private, and large data

::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>raw-data/</strong><span>Original input; preserve it unchanged.</span></div>
<div><strong>processed-data/</strong><span>Cleaned or transformed data generated by code.</span></div>
<div><strong>private-data/</strong><span>Restricted material kept in an approved location.</span></div>
<div><strong>large-files/</strong><span>Material too large for ordinary Git and GitHub use.</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
If raw data are inconvenient, write code that produces a processed version. The data README should document source, sensitivity, access limits, and AI inspection rules.

[Sources] Local template: data/readme-data.md; readme.md; usage.md; agents.md.
:::

## Code follows the stages of the analysis

<p class="figure-lead">Each stage should have recognizable inputs, outputs, and instructions.</p>

::: {.flow-figure .code-flow}
<div class="flow-row primary-flow">
<div><strong>data-processing</strong><span>raw to<br>processed</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>data-exploration</strong><span>checks<br>summaries</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>modeling-analysis</strong><span>models<br>results</span></div>
<p>→</p>
<div><strong>figures-tables</strong><span>final<br>outputs</span></div>
</div>
<div class="utility-strip"><strong>utilities/</strong><span>is optional support for repeated helper logic</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Processing creates processed data. Exploration checks it. Modeling and analysis compute results. Figures and tables prepare communication-ready artifacts. Utilities hold reusable helpers.

[Sources] Local template: usage.md; code/readme-code.md; code-guidelines.md.
:::

## Keep generated outputs separate from supporting inputs

::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>results/</strong><span>Code-generated model objects, intermediate outputs, figures, and tables.</span></div>
<div><strong>products/</strong><span>Reports, manuscripts, supplements, presentations, posters, and apps.</span></div>
<div><strong>assets/</strong><span>References, PDFs, schematics, and other stable supporting material.</span></div>
<div><strong>ai/</strong><span>AI policy, project context, guidance, and meaningful-use records.</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
Do not place manually edited results in results. Put manually created supporting files in assets and document their source.

[Sources] Local template: readme.md; assets/readme-assets.md; ai/readme-ai.md; agents.md.
:::



## A modular, staged workflow

::: {.run-sequence}
<div><span>1</span><strong>Process</strong><small>raw → processed</small></div>
<div><span>2</span><strong>Explore</strong><small>checks + summaries</small></div>
<div><span>3</span><strong>Analyze</strong><small>models + results</small></div>
<div><span>4</span><strong>Prepare</strong><small>figures + tables</small></div>
<div><span>5</span><strong>Render</strong><small>reports + slides</small></div>
:::

<p class="closing-line">Regenerate results before updating the products that use them.</p>

::: {.notes}
The example uses a documented semi-automated workflow rather than one giant pipeline. Run affected scripts before rendering the product that consumes their outputs.

[Sources] Local template: usage.md; code/readme-code.md.
:::

## Check the project before accepting or sharing it

::: {.simple-list}
<div><strong>Inputs</strong><span>Was raw data preserved and sensitive material kept in approved locations?</span></div>
<div><strong>Traceability</strong><span>Can each important output be connected to code and documented inputs?</span></div>
<div><strong>Execution</strong><span>Does the workflow run from a fresh session or clean copy?</span></div>
<div><strong>Communication</strong><span>Do instructions, paths, figures, tables, and interpretations match?</span></div>
:::

::: {.notes}
A clean run exposes hidden objects, absolute paths, missing packages, stale documentation, and manual steps. Compare outputs using criteria appropriate to the claim.

[Sources] Local template: usage.md; agents.md. ORDERly course: courses/orderly-workflows/reproducibility/reproducibility.qmd.
:::

## A useful project is easy to continue

::: {.closing-composition}
<p><strong>Current you</strong> can work efficiently.</p>
<p><strong>Future you</strong> can recover the reasoning.</p>
<p><strong>Collaborators</strong> can review and extend the work.</p>
<p><strong>Others</strong> can understand and recreate the stated result.</p>
:::

<div class="closing-mark">Make the workflow ORDERly. Let the template carry the structure.</div>

::: {.notes}
Return to the opening. The template helps implement an understandable, recorded, documented, executable workflow. AI can accelerate it when assistance remains bounded and reviewable.

[Sources] Local template: readme.md; usage.md; ai/ai-use-policy.md. ORDERly course: courses/orderly-workflows/why-orderly/why-orderly.qmd.
:::

- Update the guidelines as needed.
- Involve AI early on, make sure all is documented.
